info.title: DCRS API for the Mitra mobile app (the Audit Assistant)
info.summary: Read and change DCRS data as a signed-in person, through DCRS's own rules.
info.description: The Digital Controlled Record System's API for another server acting as a signed-in person (REQUIREMENTS §83). Sign in with POST /api/auth/login; send the session token (the dcrs_session cookie's value) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every /api/v1 call, and name the calling server in `X-Client-Name`. Everything is JSON except the PDF. The person's departments decide what may be read and changed, exactly as in DCRS itself. A session lasts until the close of the day it was started — the end of the plant's working hours (6:20 pm unless the super admin changes them) for everybody but the super admin, whose session lasts until midnight, factory time (REQUIREMENTS §84); `session.endsAt` in the sign-in answer says when. Outside the plant's working hours — before the opening, after the close, on the weekly off or a festival holiday — anybody but the super admin is refused with 403 `outside-working-hours`. WHAT MITRA DOES, FROM THE MOBILE APP (REQUIREMENTS §85): the routes tagged Mitra — documents, today's facts, records found, read, searched and printed, records opened, changed and acted on, the equipment list (F/MNT/01) and what stands out (the insights) — are answered by DCRS's own engine run on the server, so every change goes through DCRS's own checks, history and activity log, exactly as Mitra's own tools in the browser; each one maps to one of Mitra's tools (docs/chatbot-integration.md has the table). The super admin's escalations (GET /api/v1/escalations) are read from the server's own, for the super admin only. A CHANGE must be confirmed by the person first. See docs/chatbot-integration.md. NOTIFICATIONS (REQUIREMENTS §97): each person's notifications, kept by DCRS in PostgreSQL and worded on every read in the language asked (English, Hindi or Gujarati) - GET /api/v1/notifications and POST /api/v1/notifications/read - with the phone's push devices (POST and DELETE /api/v1/devices), the person's choice of what is pushed (/api/v1/notification-preferences) and a test push (POST /api/v1/notifications/test). The website reads the same at /api/notifications by its session cookie.

post.summary: Sign in as a person (DCRS's own sign-in)
post.description: The session token is the value of the `dcrs_session` cookie in the `Set-Cookie` header of the answer. It lasts until the close of the day it was started — the end of the plant's working hours for everybody but the super admin, midnight (factory time) for the super admin — and `session.endsAt` says when. Send it back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or as the cookie). Outside the plant's working hours anybody but the super admin is refused with 403 `outside-working-hours`, after the password was found right. Eight wrong passwords for one email in 10 minutes are refused with 429 for the rest of those 10 minutes.

Set-Cookie.description: dcrs_session=<token>; Max-Age=<seconds to the close of the day>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax

403.description: The account is switched off; or, for anybody but the super admin, it is outside the plant's working hours (code outside-working-hours, with the next opening).

value.error: This account has been switched off. Ask the administrator.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords for this email in 10 minutes.

post.description: Writes "Signed out" in DCRS's activity log when the session is valid. The token itself stays valid until the close of its day; the assistant should simply forget it. The body is optional, and only DCRS's own pages send it, when they sign a person out by themselves: `reason` is written in the line only where it fits the account ("end-of-working-hours" → "At the close of working hours" and "outside-working-hours" → "Outside working hours" for staff, "end-of-day" → "At the end of the day (midnight)" for the super admin; anything else is a plain sign-out), and `sessionId` names the session the page is ending: when the browser's cookie holds another session by then (signed in again in another tab), that one is left alone, with no line written.

reason.description: Why the page signed the person out by itself; written only where it fits the account. Anything else is an ordinary sign-out.

sessionId.description: The id of the session the page is ending (SessionEnd `id`). Left out, the sign-out ends whatever session the cookie holds.

post.summary: CHANGE — close a finding with a note
post.description: Exactly what DCRS's own Close button does: the finding becomes Closed with today's date (the factory's) as its date of action, and the report is saved as the page saves it (a report still Due becomes In Progress; any other keeps its status). The report's history gets an entry in the person's name with the note "Through <X-Client-Name>: <note>", and DCRS's activity log gets a "Record edited" line saying the same. Refused when the finding is already closed, when its report is verified (reopen it in DCRS with Edit first) or sent back (Resume it in DCRS first).

post.summary: CHANGE — change a record with Mitra's patch (Mitra's edit_open_record)
post.description: The patch is applied by DCRS's own engine exactly as Mitra applies it (engine/recordPatch.ts): every field checked against the form, every value normalised to what the form stores, printed and computed columns never written, one line changed only when the match names exactly one. The change is saved as the record's page saves it (a Due record becomes In Progress, computed cells worked out), with its own entry in the record's history — in the person's name, the note "Through <client>: <note>" — and the activity line "Record edited through Mitra" with the same words. What was left out is in `problems`; a patch that changes nothing is 400 nothing-changed. A record that is not open for writing (submitted, verified, sent back) is 409 needs-reopen: reopen it with a reason first (POST .../actions reopen). Ask the person first.

post.summary: CHANGE — submit, verify, send back, resume, reopen, cancel a correction, delete (Mitra's record_action)
post.description: What the record page's buttons do, through DCRS's own lifecycle and validation (engine/recordLifecycle.ts): submit (a record being filled in; DCRS's validation must pass, 409 invalid with the problems otherwise), verify or approve (a submitted record; a complaint checklist's approval stamps Approved By), send_back with a reason (a submitted record), resume (one sent back), reopen with a reason (submitted, verified or sent back — it must then be submitted and verified again), cancel_correction (puts a reopened record back exactly as it was), delete with a reason (recorded on the deletions log). Each writes its entry in the record's history in the person's name with the note "Through <client>: <reason or the action>", and the activity line the browser writes for it (Record submitted for verification, Record verified, Record sent back, Record resumed, Record reopened for correction, Correction cancelled, Record deleted) with the detail "Through <client>: …". Ask the person first. A record the assistant prepared is submitted only with "reviewed": true, sent after the person ticked "Reviewed and correct" (409 needs-review otherwise).

post.summary: CHANGE — add a photo to a record's photo or scan list (Mitra's add_photo_to_open_record)
post.description: For a record with a photo list (the complaint acknowledgement) or a scan list (the service agreement): the picture is added as Mitra adds one, with its own history entry "Through <client>: photo <fileName> added" (or the note). A JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 512 KB, its bytes checked to be what mimeType says. The server does not scale pictures (the browser scales with a canvas, which a server has not): scale to at most 1024 px on the longer side, as JPEG at 70% (about 60-150 KB), before sending. Ask the person first.

get.summary: READ — a machine on the equipment list, F/MNT/01 (what Mitra answers about a machine)
get.description: The machines on F/MNT/01, the List of Equipments & Utilities, that `q` names: a Machine No. (M-47, m47, machine no. 47), a serial number, a model or a maker (Delta 330, Brison), a place (QC, Lombardi Printing), or the person's question as they asked it. `answer` is Mitra's own reply to those words, as her rules path gives it in DCRS (engine/equipmentMasterAssistant.ts), and null when they are not a question she answers there. `machines` are the machines the words name by number, or the one a serial only it has names (`exact`); otherwise, when Mitra has no answer of her own, the machines DCRS's own search finds for the words. A model name never picks one machine, because the list repeats its model names. A line F/MNT/01 prints one column out of step (M-68) is read back in step, and says so in `note`. Without `q`: the list itself — how many machines, their numbers and the numbers it skips. The list is Maintenance's: anybody else is refused 403 not-your-department.

get.summary: READ — the super admin's escalations (the super admin only)
get.description: The escalations DCRS's server raised for the super admin (backend/escalation.ts, REQUIREMENTS §75): somebody with 3 or more late submissions, or 2 or more records never done, in the last 30 days — named by name, or as the department where several share the work — what the bell in DCRS shows. `summary` is the line Mitra adds to her live facts for the super admin in DCRS, in the same words. Each escalation says who, the counts in a sentence, the documents with the most misses and up to ten of the records behind them. They name people, so they are the super admin's alone: anybody else is refused 403 super-admin-only. Reading them changes nothing; acknowledging one stays in DCRS.

The rules are made safe before they are stored: anything not a level, a known module or an email is dropped, and emails are kept in small letters. Every change is a line of the activity log naming who changed what for whom ("Access changed", "Who answers for a document changed") and an access_changed notification to each person concerned, in the level they now have. The same item written through PUT /api/storage/access comes here too; anybody but the super admin is refused it there as well.

Never the plant's last active super admin to staff (409 last-super-admin). One line of the activity log ("Role changed") and an access_changed notification to the person. Before 9-Oct-2026 no screen could change a role: the owner's own account was stuck as staff.

Both are safe to run again (a second prepare finds nothing to prepare, and nobody is pushed twice for the same thing). For the plant's today it is that period's run, and the schedule does not repeat it. Each run is a line of the activity log. The test servers run with JOBS=0 and call this instead.

Error.description: Every refusal. `error` is a sentence to show a person; `code` is for the program. A refusal outside the staff's working hours also says when they start again (`opensAt`).

opensAt.description: Only with the code `outside-working-hours`: the next moment DCRS opens (the start of the next working day), or null when the plant's calendar has no working day in the year ahead.

id.description: The account's stable id. Never changes; keep it as the person's id in the other system.

role.description: admin is the super admin (every department).

departments.description: Department codes (QA, HR, MKT ...). An empty list means every department.

features.description: What this DCRS server has switched on.

mustChangePassword.description: True: the person must choose their own password in DCRS before the API will serve them (403 password-change-required).

FindingStatus.description: Closed or Verified as stored; otherwise Overdue when the target date is before the factory's today and no date of action is filled in; otherwise Open.

Finding.description: One internal CAPA finding (a line of a Pest Control Inspection Findings Report, owned by Quality Assurance).

id.description: Readable id: CAPA-<report date, with b, c ... for a second or third report that day>-<number>, and .2, .3 for a repeated number. Accepted in any case.

ref.description: Stable reference <record id>:<finding id>. Never changes; accepted wherever an id is.

number.description: The finding's S.No, or its place in the report when it has none.

actionDate.description: The date the action was taken (set by a close).

reportStatus.description: The report's own status in DCRS (Due, In Progress, Pending Verification, Verified, Rejected ...).

total.description: How many match, before limit and offset.

note.description: How the finding was resolved. Kept in the report's history.

Complaint.description: One customer complaint (CAPA — External: Customer Complaint Handling Checklist, F/MKT/05, owned by Marketing).

answer.description: Yes, No, a number (check point 4), or null when not answered.

PestSummary.description: The Daily Pest Control Monitoring Record (F/HR/17) of one date, as data.

status.description: The record's status in DCRS. Due or Scheduled means nobody has filled it in yet.

SessionEnd.description: When this session ends (REQUIREMENTS §84): at the close of the day it was started. Keep `endsAt` as the assistant's own session expiry.

endsAt.description: The end of today's working hours for anybody but the super admin; midnight, factory time, for the super admin (and for everybody on a server that does not enforce the hours). The dcrs_session cookie's Max-Age runs to the same moment; after it every /api/v1 call answers 401 not-signed-in.

signOutAtEnd.description: True for an account held to the plant's working hours: DCRS's own pages warn ten minutes before `endsAt` and sign the person out at it.

id.description: This session's own id. A DCRS page that ends its session by itself (at the close of the hours, at the end of the day) names it in POST /api/auth/logout, so that a tab whose clock ran late never ends a newer session of the same browser. It grants nothing by itself; the assistant can ignore it. Absent for a session started before 8-Oct-2026.

PlantHours.description: The staff's working hours and where today stands for them, worded for the person asking (since 6-Oct-2026 the hours are the STAFF's: the super admin may sign in and work at any time, and nothing here says DCRS itself is open or closed). `heldToHours` and `forYou` are in the answers for a signed-in person (sign-in, /api/auth/me, /api/v1/today), not in GET /api/auth/config.

enforced.description: False on a server started with DCRS_WORKING_HOURS=off: nobody is held to the hours.

timeZone.description: The factory's time zone, such as Asia/Kolkata.

hoursText.description: The hours in words: "Staff working hours: 8:40 am to 6:20 pm on working days. The super admin can sign in at any time."

todayText.description: Where today stands for the staff's hours, in words, such as "Today's staff hours ended at 6:20 pm; they start again on Friday 9 October at 8:40 am."

heldToHours.description: Whether the hours hold the person asking: true for staff while the server enforces them, false for the super admin.

forYou.description: For the super admin: "You are the super admin: these are the staff's hours, and you can keep working at any time." Null for staff. An assistant passes it on with hoursText and todayText, so it never tells the super admin that DCRS is closed.

DocumentBrief.description: One document (a controlled format). `route` is its page in DCRS and `link` opens it.

kind.description: log-sheet, daily-pest-monitoring, fly-catcher, service-report, gap-inspection, training-record, complaint-checklist, complaint-ack, service-agreement, pest-responsibilities, or a reference kind.

referenceOnly.description: Kept as issued: no records to fill.

documents.description: The person's own documents that match (all of them when there is no q), best first.

kept.description: Another department's documents that match: found, never opened (REQUIREMENTS §84).

notInDcrs.description: Lines of the Master List of Formats (F/SYS/02) that match and DCRS does not hold yet.

Layout.description: What the form is made of, in the keys a patch names. A log sheet: `header`, `footer` (boxes) and `columns`, each {key, label, type, options?, required?, unit?, min?, max?, printed?, computed?, readFrom?}, and `rows` {mode: timeSlots|fixedRows|free|single, slotKey?, slots?, count?}. F/HR/17: `checkpoints` {number, question, answer, noteAsks?, findingWhen?, noteChoices?, noteChoicesFrom?, noteOther?, noteChoicesSaid?}, `fields`, `lists`. Check points 8 and 9 name rodent boxes (REQUIREMENTS §104): `noteChoices` [{id, area?}] is the list a picker offers, none picked (Master Data's Active stations, else RC-1 to RC-<check point 4's count>), `noteChoicesFrom` where it came from (stations, today, last), `noteChoicesSaid` that in a line of the request's language, and `noteOther` (8 only) that a place in words may be given too. The note stays text: "RC-3, RC-17", or "RC-3; Other: near RM inward shutter". Any other form: `fields` {key, label, type, items?, parts?}. A printed or computed column, or one read from another document (readFrom), cannot be written.

patchShape.description: How a change to this kind of form is written (POST /api/v1/records/{id}/changes).

DueItem.description: One record due, overdue, coming, or waiting. `recordId` is null (and `started` false) for a sheet the calendar has not stored yet: POST /api/v1/records {documentId, date} starts it.

problems.description: needsInput only: what still stops a submit.

module.description: The module's code (QC, HR, ...) of the document; null for one in no module.

canSubmit.description: Whether this person may submit it now (their level on the document is Write or more, and the record is being filled in).

canVerify.description: Whether this person may verify it now (Write or more, and the record is submitted).

Today.description: Mitra's todays_facts: the plant's day and what is due. For a person: the documents they answer for (and, for an account nobody has described yet, every document they may fill) and the records they may verify. For the super admin: everything, with `byModule`.

upcoming.description: Due in the next three days.

readyToSubmit.description: Prepared by the assistant and passing validation.

facts.description: The same facts in words, as Mitra is given them.

byModule.description: The super admin only: the lists above counted by module.

recordId.description: Null for a sheet the calendar has not stored yet (started: false).

snippet.description: Search only: the words around what was found.

kind.description: register: only a format number was given, so its latest records are listed.

note.description: For a change through an app: "Through <X-Client-Name>: <note or the action>".

RecordDetail.description: Mitra's get_record and get_open_record in one: the record, whether it can be changed now and what can be done to it, its layout (the keys a patch names), its data in words and as stored, and its history (the last 50 entries).

editable.description: The person may write into it now: it is open for writing (Scheduled, Due or In Progress) and they have Write on the document (Edit while it is reopened for correction, REQUIREMENTS §96). Otherwise a change needs `reopen` first, or a higher level.

canReopen.description: `reopen` is among `actions`: its state allows it and the person has Edit on the document.

actions.description: What POST .../actions can do to it now, for this person: the steps its state allows that their level allows too (Write: submit, verify, send_back, resume; Edit: reopen, cancel_correction, delete). A person who only reads the document is given none.

canSubmit.description: It is open for writing and the person may submit it (Write or more on the document), as GET /api/v1/today's items say.

canVerify.description: It is waiting for verification and the person may verify or send it back (Write or more on the document).

problems.description: While the person may write it: what still stops a submit, in DCRS's own words (the submit's own checks). Empty when it may be submitted, and when the person may not write it.

waiting.description: While the person may write it: how many entries wait before it is ready for their OK. The submit's checks, and for a log sheet nothing has been observed on, each observation of its first line (REQUIREMENTS §98: a record holding only its lines and its date is never ready).

correction.description: Set while it is reopened for correction: reason, by, at, fromStatus.

prepared.description: Prepared by the assistant (REQUIREMENTS §98: the known parts only, never a reading): at, notes (what was written in, from where, and what is left for the person), basedOn.

photos.description: Which picture list it has, if any (POST .../photos).

linked.description: F/MNT/03 only: the Actual dates read from each machine's F/MNT/02 (not stored on the sheet).

documentId.description: The document's id or its format number.

date.description: The record's date; today (the server's) when left out.

created.description: True when this call stored the record (201); false when it was already on file (200).

editable.description: As RecordDetail.editable: the person may write into it now.

actions.description: As RecordDetail.actions: what this person may do to it now.

patch.description: Mitra's patch (engine/recordPatch.ts applyAssistantPatch). A field: {"<key>": value}. A log sheet: {"header": {"<box key>": value}, "itemEdits": [{"collection": "rows", "match": {"<slot key>": "10:00"} or {"row": 2}, "set": {"<column key>": value}}]}, or "rows" given in full. F/HR/17: {"checkpoints": {"<n>": value or {value, note}}}. Values are read as the form stores them ("yes" -> Yes, "9.15 am" -> 09:15, "20.4" -> 20.4, a select's option however it is cased); a field the form does not have, a printed or computed column, or a value it cannot hold is left out and said in `problems`.

note.description: Why, in the person's words: the history says "Through <client>: <note>".

problems.description: What was left out, and why.

action.description: approve is verify (a complaint checklist's approval stamps Approved By).

reason.description: Needed for send_back, reopen and delete.

reviewed.description: submit only: true once the person has ticked "Reviewed and correct" on the review screen. A record the assistant prepared (its `prepared` stamp) is refused with 409 needs-review without it (REQUIREMENTS §62, §97); with it, the history says "Through <client>: Submitted from the phone after review".

dataBase64.description: The picture's bytes in base64 (a data: prefix is allowed), at most 512 KB decoded. DCRS keeps photos scaled to at most 1024 px on the longer side, as JPEG at 70% — scale before sending, as the server does not.

evidence.description: One fact per line, records tagged [rec:<id>] — what Mitra's model is given to answer from.

Machine.description: One line of F/MNT/01 as Mitra reads it: put back in step where the list prints it one column out (then `note` says so), and the list's "NA" and "-" as null.

machineNo.description: M-47: the machine is its number.

section.description: The list's own "Department" column: a section of the plant (Flexo, Common), not one of DCRS's departments.

summary.description: Number, what it is, model, where it stands.

note.description: Only for a line the list prints one column out of step: what was done, and to confirm it against the plate.

list.description: F/MNT/01 itself: the record the machines are read from, how many there are, their numbers and the numbers it skips.

answer.description: Mitra's own reply to the words, as her rules path gives it in DCRS; null when they are not a question she answers there.

exact.description: The Machine No. the words name without doubt: a number, or a serial only one machine has.

rule.description: Which insight rule found it (A1, B2, M6, …).

evidence.description: Up to five of the records it was read from, newest first.

headline.description: The line Mitra is given with every message in DCRS: the counts by severity and the most severe titles.

period.description: The ISO week it belongs to, such as 2026-W40.

summary.description: The line Mitra adds for the super admin in DCRS, or that nothing is waiting.

waiting.description: How many are not yet acknowledged.

NotificationKind.description: ready: a record the assistant prepared that passes DCRS's checks - review it, then submit. needs_input: a record that is open and waits for a person's readings (`count` says how many things still stop a submit). due: due today and not started. upcoming: a heads-up by the document's frequency (the working day before for weekly and fortnightly, three days before for monthly, quarterly and yearly). overdue: still open after its day (`daysLate`), one item per record, updated daily. verify: a submitted record waiting for verification, for those with Write on the document other than the submitter. sent_back: a record sent back, for the person who submitted it, with the `reason`. boss_summary: the super admin's morning and evening counts by module (`modules`). escalation: one of the super admin's escalations (REQUIREMENTS §75), until it is acknowledged. access_changed: the super admin changed what this person may do.

module.description: The module's code: QC, HR, SYS, MNT, PRD, PUR, STR, MKT, DISP or QA.

notSubmitted.description: Due today and not yet submitted.

NotificationData.description: What the notification is about, in language-neutral facts: the title and body are worded from these on every read. Never a record's values. `subject`, `late`, `neverDone`, `level`, `by` and `part` were added to the shared contract (docs/chatbot-integration.md, Notification contract changes).

recordId.description: The record to open (mitra://task/<recordId>); absent for a sheet not started yet.

count.description: needs_input: how many things still stop a submit (the readings to enter).

daysLate.description: overdue: whole days after the day it had to be in.

reason.description: sent_back: what must be put right, as the verifier wrote it.

subject.description: escalation: the person or the department escalated.

late.description: escalation: late submissions in the last 30 days.

neverDone.description: escalation: records never done in the last 30 days.

level.description: access_changed: the level the person now has.

by.description: verify: who submitted it; sent_back: who sent it back; access_changed: who changed it.

part.description: boss_summary: which of the day's two summaries.

title.description: Worded in the language asked (?lang=en|hi|gu), never from stored text.

resolvedAt.description: When the item stopped needing the person (the record moved on); null while it is open.

unread.description: Open items not yet read (the bell's count).

open.description: Open items, read or not (the app's badge).

ReadRequest.description: Either ids (at most 500) or all: true.

token.description: The Expo push token, ExponentPushToken[...] (or ExpoPushToken[...]).

language.description: The language this phone's pushes are worded in.

kinds.description: A kind set to false is not pushed (it still reaches the inbox). Kinds left out keep their setting; GET answers every kind.

reminders.description: The phone's own daily reminders (08:50 and 17:30 on working days). Absent until the person chooses.

sent.description: How many of the caller's phones Expo's push service accepted the test for.

reason.description: When nothing was sent: why, in words (push switched off on this server, no phone registered). Added to the shared contract (Notification contract changes).

AccessRules.description: What the super admin has set (frontend/src/engine/accessRules.ts AccessRules): `people` by lower-cased email, each with `modules` and `documents` levels; `responsibility` by document id, the emails who answer for it.

version.description: The stored version; send it back as baseVersion.

AccessLevelRefusal.description: A step the person's access level on the document does not allow (REQUIREMENTS §96). `error` is the website's own sentence, in the language X-Language asks for.

level.description: The level the person has on the document.

recordId.description: The record, when the step was on one already stored.

job.description: morning-prepare: the day's records prepared on the server (the known parts only). notify: each person's notifications worked out and their phones pushed. escalation and weekly-digest: the super admin's (REQUIREMENTS §75).

today.description: A day of the caller's own (a test's); left out, the plant's today.

time.description: The moment, plant time, the notification jobs are worked out at; left out, now.

outcome.description: How it went, in a line (the activity log has the same).

result.description: The job's own figures. morning-prepare: date, prepared, sheetsMade, modules [{module, count}], records. notify: date, time, planned, written, resolved, escalations, cleaned, push.

claimed.description: The period this run stood for (the schedule then leaves it alone), or null for a day of the caller's own or one already run.
